key: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutman. To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Matarisvan.
s: Just after a riddle on the four divisions of speech, in a long hymn of riddles, the singer turns to the names of the gods; Sāyaṇa, on 1.164.46, reads the One as the Sun, not other than Brahman and so the self of all, and Yāska, Nirukta 7.18, as this very Agni, the great self.

evidence.words: अमुमेवादित्यम् “एकम् एव वस्तुतः सन्तं “विप्राः मेधाविनो देवतातत्वविदः “बहुधा “वदन्ति । तत्तत्कार्यकारणेन इन्द्राद्यात्मानं वदन्ति … सूर्यस्य ब्रह्मणोऽनन्यत्वेन सार्वात्म्यमुक्तं भवति … इममेवाग्निं महान्तमात्मानमेकमात्मानं बहुधा मेधाविनो वदन्ति … The wise speak of this very Agni, [and] the great self, in various ways, as Indra, Mitra, Yaruna, Agni, and the divine Garutman … He to whom the hymn is addressed and the oblation is ottered, is this very (terrestrial) Agni.
evidence.gloss: [Sāyaṇa:] That very Sun, being in truth one, the ‘sages’, the wise who know the truth of the deities, ‘speak of in many ways’: by reason of his several works they speak of him as Indra and the rest … by the Sun’s being not other than Brahman, his being the self of all is declared … [Yāska, Nirukta 7.18, in his Sanskrit as Sāyaṇa quotes it:] this very Agni, the great self, the one self, the wise speak of in many ways … [Yāska in Sarup’s English, OCR as printed, Yaruna for Varuna and ottered for offered:] the wise speak of this very Agni, the great self, in various ways … he to whom the hymn is addressed and the oblation offered is this very (terrestrial) Agni.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.164.46, at [163,46]), the whole verse. Plain sense faithful: 1.164.45 is the riddle of speech in four divisions and 1.164 is the long riddle hymn; no four-word run from the key. Sāyaṇa on 1.164.46 takes the one as amum ādityam (the Sun), called Indra and the rest by his several works, and says the Sun’s non-difference from Brahman (brahmaṇo ’nanyatvena) declares his being the self of all (sārvātmyam). Yāska, whom the Nirukta itself (7.18, by Sarup’s list) and Sāyaṇa’s quotation both give, reads imam evāgniṃ mahāntam ātmānam, this very Agni the great self, and adds that it is the terrestrial Agni. Two commentators are named because they genuinely differ (Sun against Agni); Wilson’s note names the same difference. The sentence names it without resolving it. Sarup’s bracketed [and] is his, and the sentence follows the Sanskrit apposition instead.
